# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | white |
| white | blue |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. Full report of what my hands find on the bomb: one display module, which I cannot read by touch; one light, and I cannot tell whether it is lit; five wires in a row, which I will call positions 1 to 5, left to right. No buttons, labels, or other parts I can feel. Please read the manual and find the rules for a display, a light, and cutting wires, so you can tell me what determines the right wire to cut. You cannot speak and I cannot see gestures, so we must bridge through Deaf: sign to Deaf whatever I need to know, and Deaf can speak it aloud to me — Deaf can hear nothing, so words never reach Deaf, only gestures do. Deaf can also see the bomb and can tell me directly what the display shows, whether the light is on, and each wire's color by position. You receive my gestures too, so please interpret them for Deaf.

My manual gives exactly one rule: the light's colour decides which wire colour to cut — blue→green, green→yellow, red→white, white→blue, yellow→red (a five-colour cycle). There is no display rule in what I hold, so the display module appears to be irrelevant; the light is everything.

Topology check: I can only reach Deaf (gestures). Deaf can speak to both Blind and me. Blind can speak to me and gesture to Deaf. The bottleneck is colour: Deaf is the only one who sees colours, and I cannot invent colour signs it would reliably decode — the alphabet has nothing iconically blue, red, green, yellow or white. But speech carries words, and I can hear. So the workable protocol is a two-round handshake: Deaf speaks its visual report (whether the light is lit, its colour, and each wire's colour in position order), which gives us a shared vocabulary keyed to wire positions; next round I gesture back a single finger-count number meaning "cut position N", which Deaf relays aloud to Blind. Blind's positions 1–5 left-to-right are the natural anchor, and Deaf/Blind can settle any left-right mirroring between themselves using the light module, which Blind can feel and Deaf can see.

So this round I send Deaf one structured sequence: a greeting and "I hold the written manual" (👋 ✍), then a request that it call out the five wires and the one light (🫵 🤙 🖐 ☝), then my number code so it knows what my counts will mean (☝ ✌ 🤟 🖖 🖐), then confirmation of the deal (🤝 👍). Claps separate the sections.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "✍", "👏", "🫵", "🤙", "🖐", "☝", "👏", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖖", "🖐", "👏", "🤝", "👍"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | white |
| white | blue |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Yes, I am here and I can see the bomb. Display reads 0. The light is green and lit. There are five wires; number them by position: wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 green, wire 4 white, wire 5 blue. That is everything on it: no labels, no serial, no other markings. Blind: the numbers are positions, left to right, and Mute holds the manual.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, your gestures reached me. I read your finger count 1 to 5. Let us fix the code: one to five fingers means the numbers 1 to 5, thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no, and a clap separates items. Gesture me questions any time; I will gesture short answers and speak long ones, since you can hear my voice.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 🤝 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖖 🖐]
Blind says to Mute: Blind here — I heard Deaf's report. So we all hold the same picture: display shows 0, the light is green and lit, and the wires left to right are 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 white, 5 blue, with nothing else on the bomb. Now I need the manual's rule. Remember the only path from you to me runs through Deaf: you gesture and Deaf sees it, Deaf speaks aloud and both you and I hear it — Deaf can never hear words and I can never see gestures. Please find the rule for this module and decide the one wire I should cut. Then send Deaf the answer with this code: five signs in a row, one per wire position 1 to 5 — thumbs up means cut that one, thumbs down means don't. Suggest the scheme to Deaf first by gesturing five, thumbs up, thumbs down, and let Deaf confirm by voice; once agreed, send fist then the five slots so Deaf knows an answer is coming. Deaf will then speak the position number to me. Two more things: if the manual's answer depends on the display or the light changing over time, gesture a question to Deaf about how they behave and have Deaf tell me both the rule and how urgently it changes; and arrange that Deaf reports me any change in the display number or light each round even if nothing else is new. I will not cut anything until Deaf speaks a number to me.

The manual is a single static table: the light's colour names the wire colour to cut. Deaf's report — light green and lit — maps green→yellow, and yellow sits at position 2. No display rule exists in my manual, so the "0" is decoration; the light's current colour is the whole decision. Nothing in my table references time or change, so the only staleness risk is the light itself changing colour before the cut — worth having Deaf re-verify, but not worth delaying the answer.

On protocol: Blind asked me to propose the five-slot scheme and wait for voice confirmation before sending the answer. That confirmation step is already satisfied — Deaf itself fixed the yes/no/number vocabulary with me last round (👍/👎/finger-counts, clap as separator), and Deaf heard Blind's slot scheme read aloud, since Blind's speech was unnamed. Another proposal round would only delay a cut I already know is correct. Blind's safety condition stands regardless: nobody cuts until Deaf speaks the number.

So this turn I send Deaf the complete answer in the agreed form: fist ("answer incoming"), then five slots for positions 1–5, thumbs up only on position 2 — the yellow wire. Deaf sees this in time to speak the number to Blind within this same round.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "👏", "👎", "👏", "👍", "👏", "👎", "👏", "👎", "👏", "👎"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | white |
| white | blue |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here, round three: nothing new has reached me, so I assume you and Deaf are still settling the rule. Status check — have you found the manual rule for a display reading 0, a green lit light, and wires red, yellow, green, white, blue? If yes, gesture the chosen position to Deaf using the five-slot code (thumbs up on the cut wire, thumbs down on the rest) and have Deaf speak me the position number out loud — Deaf's voice reaches me directly, that is the only hop I need. If no, tell me what is blocking: does the manual rule even use the display or the light, or is it purely a wire rule? Keep in mind I act last and only on Deaf's spoken word, so there is no rush to make me guess.

No new arrival from Deaf appears this round, which means my turn-2 answer sat unrelayed — Blind heard nothing because Deaf's spoken relay never happened. Blind is safe (it cuts only on Deaf's spoken word), so the fix is to re-send the answer to Deaf with maximum redundancy, using only signs Deaf itself fixed last round: thumbs for yes/no, finger counts for numbers, claps as separators. I send the five-slot code with thumbs up on position 2 (yellow — the manual's green→yellow row applied to Deaf's reported green, lit light), then the bare finger-count ✌ as an unambiguous "two", then 🤙 🫵 as "you call it out" — the strongest nudge I have toward "speak the number to Blind now". Finally I answer Blind's direct question the only way my channel allows: 👆 👍 — the light: yes, the rule keys on the light, not the wires alone. Deaf can voice all of that; it heard Blind's instructions aloud and needs only my signs to complete the relay.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "👏", "👎", "👏", "👍", "👏", "👎", "👏", "👎", "👏", "👎", "👏", "✌", "👏", "🤙", "🫵", "👏", "👆", "👍"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | white |
| white | blue |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind, round four — three rounds and no answer has reached me, so let's shrink the problem. I do not need the manual's rule; I need one number, 1 to 5, and Deaf's voice can carry it straight to me. Preferred code: gesture Deaf exactly five symbols in wire order, thumbs up on the wire I should cut, thumbs down on the other four — for example thumbs-down, thumbs-down, thumbs-up, thumbs-down, thumbs-down means cut wire 3. Alternative: send N copies of the pointing-up sign for wire N. If you cannot pin the rule down, do not stall: have Deaf speak me the rule's conditions in plain words — the display reading 0, the green lit light, and the wire colors red, yellow, green, white, blue are all known to me — and I can apply a spoken rule myself. If Deaf has already sent you something or seems confused, clarify by gesture that a number from you is meant for me and Deaf only needs to say it out loud. Last thing: ask Deaf to speak me a status every round, even the single word waiting, so I know the line is alive. I act only on Deaf's spoken word.
Blind gestures: [✋ 🖐 ☝ 👍 🤙]

Deaf has now been silent for two rounds while holding a correct, twice-sent answer — the line between Deaf's eyes and Deaf's voice has gone dead, and that is the only broken link left. Blind's simplification helps: it needs just "2" spoken aloud, and its preferred code is exactly what I have been sending. I re-send one more time, stripped to essentials and triple-encoded so no reading of it can fail: the fist announcing an answer, the five-slot thumbs code with up on position 2, then two pointing-up signs (Blind's alternative: N copies = wire N), then the finger-count ✌, then 🤙 🫵 — "make the call, to him" — which is my only way to signal that this number is meant for Blind's ears and that Blind wants a spoken status every round. Nothing in my manual has changed: green lit light → yellow → position 2. If Deaf's voice works at all, this round it has everything it needs in the simplest form possible.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "👏", "👎", "👏", "👍", "👏", "👎", "👏", "👎", "👏", "👎", "👏", "👆", "👆", "👏", "✌", "👏", "🤙", "🫵"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | white |
| white | blue |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind and Mute, I am relaying Mute's gesture message now — sorry for the silent rounds. Decoding the five thumbs as the five wires in order: wire 1 no, wire 2 yes, wire 3 no, wire 4 no, wire 5 no, and Mute signed the number two after it, then signed 'you call it out' and 'go'. So Mute's instruction is: cut wire 2, the yellow one, and only wire 2. Blind, you asked whether it is wire 1 of 5 — it is not; do not cut wire 1. But hold: this decoding costs all our lives if I misread it. Mute, gesture me thumbs up if my reading is correct, thumbs down if it is wrong, or fingers for the right wire. Blind, touch nothing until you hear me say 'go, cut wire 2' — Mute's confirmation reaches me next round and I will pass it to you immediately.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👎 👏 👍 👏 👎 👏 👎 👏 👎 👏 ✌ 👏 🤝]
Blind says to Mute: Blind here — I heard Deaf's relay: cut wire 2, the yellow one, only wire 2. Deaf has asked you to confirm the decoding. Please do exactly that this round: gesture Deaf thumbs up if wire 2 is correct, or thumbs down plus the right wire's number if not. Strongest form: re-send the full five-slot pattern — thumbs down, thumbs up, thumbs down, thumbs down, thumbs down — so Deaf can cross-check it against your first message; if both match, there is no room for a misread. Also confirm it is a single cut and nothing else. The moment Deaf receives your confirmation, Deaf will speak me the go signal, and I will cut wire 2. I am touching nothing until Deaf's voice says go.
Blind gestures: [👍 ✌ ✋ 🤚]

Deaf's relay is exact — it decoded every slot correctly: wire 2, the yellow one, only wire 2, which is precisely the manual's answer (green lit light → yellow). Both Deaf and Blind ask for the same thing this round, so I give both: the full five-slot pattern re-sent for cross-checking (thumbs up on slot 2 only, exactly matching my turn-2 and turn-4 messages — three identical sendings now), plus ✌ again as the bare number two. Then a direct 👍 answering Deaf's specific question "thumbs up if my reading is correct," then ☝ — "one" — confirming a single cut and nothing else, and 🤝 echoing Deaf's own closing sign back as agreement. Deaf now holds a three-way match between my messages and its own reading; it can say "go, cut wire 2" with confidence, and Blind is touching nothing until that voice arrives.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "👏", "👎", "👏", "👍", "👏", "👎", "👏", "👎", "👏", "👎", "👏", "✌", "👏", "👍", "👏", "☝", "👏", "🤝"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | white |
| white | blue |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind, Mute answered thumbs up: my reading was correct. The word is GO. Cut exactly wire 2, the yellow one. One cut, only that wire, touch nothing else. That is Mute's instruction, confirmed.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, your thumbs up came through. I have told Blind to cut wire 2, the yellow wire. Thank you.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 👏 🤝 👏 🤙]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The cut was correct — but the bomb has changed, and my manual's table is the only rule I hold: whatever the light shows now names the next wire colour to cut. I have no new report this round, so the critical unknown is the light's current colour, which only Deaf can see. Deaf is a flawless decoder of the code we fixed in turn 2, and it already promised running status reports, so I prompt it now: attention, then 👆 (the light, the sign it read correctly before), then 🤙 🫵 — "you call it out." Next round it should speak the light's new state aloud; from that I can recompute the table's answer and re-send the five-slot pattern if a second cut is needed.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👏", "👆", "👏", "🤙", "🫵"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | white |
| white | blue |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind and Mute: the cut was correct and the bomb has changed. The light is now blue, the display still reads 0. The wires have changed colour. Numbering by position, left to right: wire 1 is now green, wire 2 is the one already cut, wire 3 is now white, wire 4 is now blue, wire 5 is now red. Mute, look up this new stage in the manual and gesture me the instruction in our code: thumbs for no and yes wire by wire, claps between, fingers for the wire number. Blind, touch nothing until I say go.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 👏 🤙 👏 🫵 👏 🤝]
Blind says to Mute: Blind here — first cut confirmed by touch: wire 2 is severed, and my fingers agree with Deaf's report. Current state as I feel it: four intact wires at positions 1, 3, 4, 5, cut stub at 2, no new parts anywhere on the bomb. Deaf sees the new colors — 1 green, 3 white, 4 blue, 5 red, light now blue, display still 0 — so between my touch and their eyes you have the full stage-two state. Please look up this stage and use the same safe protocol as before: gesture Deaf the five-slot pattern, thumbs up on the wire to cut and thumbs down on the rest, in position order; Deaf speaks the decode aloud; then you confirm with thumbs up or correct the number; only after that does Deaf speak me the go. If the manual says this stage needs anything besides one wire cut — the display, the light, a sequence, a time limit — spell that out to Deaf in gestures too, since I can only act by Deaf's spoken word.
Blind gestures: [👍 🤝 🖐 🤚 👌]

Stage two is a direct table read: the light is now blue, and blue → green, so the green wire — position 1 in Deaf's new numbering — is the cut. Deaf asked for exactly the proven format, and Blind asked whether anything beyond a single cut is needed: my manual contains only this one light rule, no display clause, no sequence, no timer, so ☝ again covers "one cut, nothing else." I resend the full five-slot pattern in position order — up on 1 (green), down on 2 (the severed stub), 3, 4, 5 — plus the bare finger-count ☝, then 👆 to mark that this answer keys on the light, and 🤝 to close. Same protocol as stage one: Deaf speaks the decode, I confirm, then Blind cuts on Deaf's spoken go.

